label: SIMULATION/known-truth equation suite (no causal claims)
verdict_rule: status = the script's own decision_rule.PASS (not returncode==0); status is PASS / RULE_FAIL / NO_RULE / FAIL(execution)

stdout_tail: PLAIN: Family income raises schooling demand in every budget specification (income elasticity range 0.16-1.52), forgone earnings reduce it, and at zero schooling effect on births the raw schooling-births association is absorbed once income is controlled. This is a demonstration of budget arithmetic, not an estimate of any country's demand.
RULE: {'affordability_positive_across_specs': True, 'forgone_earnings_reduces_schooling': True, 'zero_signal_association_absorbed_by_income': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: A universal per-student subsidy is pro-rich in this model (concentration index 0.408 vs -0.476 for means-testing) because enrolment rises with income; the investment arithmetic gives a positive NPV at 5% and an IRR of 25.0%. These are arithmetic consequences of the stated assumptions, not policy estimates.
RULE: {'universal_more_pro_rich_than_means_tested': True, 'npv_positive_at_5pct': True, 'irr_above_5pct': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: In the CES world the ability-controlled interaction is positive (0.002) and the CES fit beats Cobb-Douglas on RMSE (0.291 vs 0.549); in the linear null world the controlled interaction is near zero (0.005). This is a demonstration about estimators, not evidence about any school system.

RULE: {'linear_world_interaction_oracle_CI_includes_0': True, 'complementary_world_interaction_oracle_positive': True, 'rho_recovered_within_0.10_in_half_reps': True, 'ces_beats_cd_rmse_in_complementary_world': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: A score bar admits rich pupils at a higher rate (gap 0.551); a reserved quota narrows the gap (0.087) but does NOT flip its sign, so the pre-declared 'quota flips the gap' rule FAILS, and a contest in which richer pupils invest more effort widens it further (0.764). The quota changes who is admitted, not how much anyone learns — this is a rationing demonstration, not an evaluation of any admissions policy.
RULE: {'baseline_gap_positive': True, 'quota_flips_gap_negative': False, 'contest_widens_gap': True, 'PASS': False}

PLAIN: Under the stipulated ability-bias DGP the naive regression overstates the return (mean bias 0.033) while 2SLS is much closer (mean bias 0.003); with no ability bias both recover the 9% return. This is a demonstration of the estimator, not an estimate of any real return.
RULE: {'bias_world_naive_biased': True, 'bias_world_iv_bias_smaller': True, 'null_world_naive_close': True, 'null_world_iv_close': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: Education raises the migration probability in every specification (marginal effect range 0.0077-0.0137) and migrants are more educated than stayers; networks slightly REDUCE the estimated marginal effect (0.0077 with vs 0.0137 without), so the ad hoc 'networks increase the effect' criterion FAILS. MASSENG v5 does not model rural-urban migration, so this is a synthetic demonstration of the equation, not a model output.
RULE: {'education_positive_in_every_spec': True, 'network_spec_effect_larger_than_no_network': False, 'PASS': False}

PLAIN: In the null world the intergenerational elasticity is indistinguishable from zero (90% CI -0.01 to 0.01); in the persistent world it is 0.45 and the Theil decomposition puts 0.10 of inequality between parent-education groups. The elasticity, the Gini and the transition matrix are different summaries of the same synthetic process, not interchangeable evidence.
RULE: {'null_elasticity_ci_includes_0': True, 'persistent_elasticity_positive': True, 'theil_between_positive': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: In the clean world the convergence coefficient is recovered and the human-capital term is zero; with an omitted TFP term correlated with human capital the human-capital coefficient is inflated (0.5363 vs -0.0162), so a positive growth coefficient is not evidence of a causal human-capital effect.
RULE: {'clean_lambda_near_truth': False, 'confound_inflates_beta_H': True, 'nelson_phelps_interaction_positive': True, 'PASS': False}

PLAIN: Each design recovers its target in its own known-truth world and is near zero in the no-effect control; the naive estimators are biased in the stated violation worlds (IV 1.49 vs OLS 1.76 against a true 1.5; TWFE bias -1.14 vs the group-time estimator -0.02). This is a demonstration of the designs, not an estimate of any real programme.
RULE: {'null_twfe_near_zero': True, 'null_iv_near_zero': True, 'null_rd_near_zero': True, 'null_sc_near_zero': True, 'iv_closer_than_ols': True, 'PASS': True}

PLAIN: Tutoring behaves as one exams-shadow module for demand: on the log1p scale (same units as the 0.8 truth) the two-part model is closer than the Tobit (0.74 vs 1.39). The log1p Tobit does NOT recover the truth, so the dropped pre-registered single-process rule fails (Tobit within-0.15 share 0.00). On inequality the own-teacher ban does NOT raise the learning Gini once the Gini is computed on a strictly positive level domain: in this reduced production model there is no substitution margin, so removing tutoring lowers the Gini in every CES/retention specification (delta range -0.065..-0.036). The illustrative model is far from Bray's targets (max |z| = 10.6), so nothing here is a fit to a real shadow-education system.
